title: Rational-algebraic simple overfield for a p-adic algebraic element
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, write $k=\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-numbers], and let $\Omega/k$ be an algebraic closure [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. For every $x\in\Omega$ there is $b\in\Omega$ algebraic over $\mathbf Q$ [def-weil-algebraic-element] such that $x\in k(b)$, where $k(b)\subseteq\Omega$ is the smallest subfield containing $k$ and $b$.

source.place: Proposition 1.1.9, first bullet, p. 3: arithmetic input to countability of finite extensions. Exact project source proof: WeilConjectures/NumberTheory/Padics/Extension.lean:76–127, PadicAlgCl.exists_isAlgebraic_mem_adjoin_simple (declaration at line 82), using rational approximation, continuity of roots, and Krasner. Arbitrary algebraic closure follows by the field isomorphism of def-weil-algebraic-closure.

proof.text: Put $k=\mathbf Q_\ell$. By [def-weil-l-adic-numbers], $k$ is complete, nonarchimedean and characteristic zero; its norm is nontrivial because $|\ell|_\ell=\ell^{-1}\ne1$. The same definition makes $k$ the completion of $\mathbf Q$, so $\mathbf Q$ is dense in $k$: a Cauchy sequence representing any $a\in k$ has rational terms arbitrarily close to $a$. The given $\Omega/k$ is algebraic by [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Apply [lem-trf-spectral-norm-algebraic-extension] with $F=k$, $L=\Omega$ to equip this field with a multiplicative nonarchimedean norm extending that of $k$.

source.place: Proposition 1.1.9, first bullet, p. 3; explicit argument from project Extension.lean:82–127.

proof.text: Fix $x\in\Omega$. It is algebraic over $k$ by [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Take its monic irreducible minimal polynomial $f\in k[T]$ with $f(x)=0$, as in [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. Its degree $n$ is positive, since a monic constant would be $1$ and could not vanish. Since $k$ has characteristic zero, the leading coefficient of $f'$ is $n\ne0$, so $f'\ne0$. Hence [lem-trf-irreducible-separable-derivative] gives that $f$ is separable. By [lem-pc-separable-polynomial-distinct-roots-alg-closed], $f$ has exactly $n$ distinct roots in $\Omega$ and splits there.

source.place: Proposition 1.1.9, first bullet, p. 3; explicit argument from project Extension.lean:82–127.

proof.text: Let $S$ be the roots of $f$ in $\Omega$ other than $x$. It is finite by step 2. If $S=\varnothing$, set $\delta=1$; otherwise let $\delta$ be the minimum of the finite nonempty set $\{\|x-y\|:y\in S\}$. Each value is positive, so $\delta>0$, and $\delta\leq\|x-y\|$ for every $y\in S$. This includes $n=1$ without taking a minimum of an empty set.

source.place: Proposition 1.1.9, first bullet, p. 3; explicit argument from project Extension.lean:82–127.

proof.text: Set $M=\max\{\|x\|,1\}$ and $\varepsilon=(\delta/M)^n/(n+1)>0$. Apply [lem-sfb-monic-dense-approximation] to $\mathbf Q\subseteq k$, $f$ and this $\varepsilon$. It supplies a monic $g\in\mathbf Q[T]$ of degree $n$ whose image $h\in k[T]$ satisfies $\|h_i-f_i\|<\varepsilon$ for every $i$. Field inclusions preserve its leading coefficient $1$ and its zero coefficients above degree $n$, so $h$ is also monic of degree $n$.

source.place: Proposition 1.1.9, first bullet, p. 3; explicit argument from project Extension.lean:82–127.

proof.text:
The image of $h$ in $\Omega[T]$ splits by induction on its degree: degree zero is the monic polynomial $1$, an empty product; in positive degree [def-weil-algebraic-closure] gives a root $a$, and division by $T-a$ has remainder $h(a)=0$, leaving a monic quotient of degree one less. Thus induction factors it completely. Apply [lem-sfb-roots-coefficient-proximity] over $k\subseteq\Omega$ to $f,h,x,\varepsilon$. The norm extension is step 1, and the root, monicity, common positive degree and coefficient bound are steps 2 and 4. We obtain $b\in\Omega$ with $h(b)=0$ and
$$\|x-b\|<((n+1)\varepsilon)^{1/n}M=((\delta/M)^n)^{1/n}M=\delta,$$
since $M\geq1$, $\delta>0$ and $n\geq1$.

source.place: Proposition 1.1.9, first bullet, p. 3; explicit argument from project Extension.lean:82–127.

proof.text: For this $b$, $g(b)=h(b)=0$: writing $g=\sum_i q_iT^i$, both evaluations are $\sum_i q_i b^i$ in $\Omega$, because $\mathbf Q\to k\to\Omega$ is the prime-field inclusion. The polynomial $g$ is nonzero since it is monic, so $b$ is algebraic over $\mathbf Q$ by [def-weil-algebraic-element].

source.place: Proposition 1.1.9, first bullet, p. 3; explicit argument from project Extension.lean:82–127.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-complete-normed-krasner] with $K=k$, $L=\Omega$ and $x,b$. Steps 1–2 give its base, extension, separability and splitting hypotheses. For every root $y\ne x$, steps 3 and 5 give $\|x-b\|<\delta\leq\|x-y\|$. The lemma yields $x\in k(b)$. Together with step 6 this proves the statement for the originally given $\Omega$.

I read the item and all three new nodes in full. The item statement is unchanged and true; edge case: if x is in Q_l but transcendental over Q, b=0 works because k(b) contains k. It is not a re-split item: the base had a statement only. L19 Prop 1.1.9 (p.3) only invokes countability, so proof_origin agent is correct. The project theorem PadicAlgCl.exists_isAlgebraic_mem_adjoin_simple is stated for the fixed model only, so it stays as a lean_candidate. Steps: (1) Q_l is complete, nonarchimedean and nontrivial (|l|=1/l), with Q dense in it; lem-trf-spectral-norm-algebraic-extension gives an extending multiplicative norm on Omega. (2) The minimal polynomial has f' != 0 in characteristic 0, so it is separable by lem-trf-irreducible-separable-derivative; lem-pc-separable-polynomial-distinct-roots-alg-closed gives the distinct roots and the splitting. (3) delta is the minimum root gap, with an explicit empty-set branch. (4) I checked the approximation with eps=(delta/M)^n/(n+1). (5) The proximity bound ((n+1)eps)^(1/n)M equals delta. (6) g(b)=0 with g monic, so b is algebraic over Q. (7) Krasner gives x in k(b). Every hypothesis matches the Mathlib source I read: Approximation.lean:43-60 and 111-140, Krasner.lean:40-140 (the of_completeSpace instance needs NontriviallyNormedField, CompleteSpace, IsUltrametricDist, NormedAlgebra and Algebra.IsAlgebraic; IsConjRoot corresponds to the roots of the minimal polynomial). All three new nodes are exact or one-line Mathlib leaves, self-contained, strictly smaller than the item, and none restates a clause of it. The rg -L duplicate search found only lem-per-henselian-krasner-neighbourhood, lem-per-henselian-simple-root-stability and lem-trf-separable-monic-approximation, each a different statement and not a one-line specialization. Neither is part of the trace formula or Poincare duality or their proofs, so both are accepted. No SGA citations and no tool_uses needed.
